idiom_name: test-only class implementing the interface over HashMap with a List<Operation> journal
implementation_notes: Implement the collaborator interface by hand in the test source set: a HashMap (or ConcurrentHashMap) supplies the working behaviour and a List of typed records supplies the journal, exposed through a package-private or otherwise test-visible accessor; nothing in the JDK replaces this compound. Mockito records interactions on mocks and spies - verify(), ArgumentCaptor, InOrder - without implementing behaviour, so it covers the spy and mock rows and is the right tool when only the interaction matters. List.copyOf/List.of give cheap immutable snapshots of the journal, and a fresh fake in @BeforeEach (or an explicit clear) avoids an instance field that would otherwise survive between test methods. Prefer record classes for journal entries, since value equality is what assertions want.
pitfalls: HashMap and ArrayList are not thread-safe; a fake exercised from an executor needs ConcurrentHashMap plus a synchronized journal, or the recorded trace is silently corrupted.
A fake kept in an instance field of the test class survives between @Test methods - re-create it in @BeforeEach.
Recording whole argument objects lets later mutation of a mutable argument rewrite the recorded history; snapshot or copy the values that matter.
